title: Zscaler CEO Pushes Back On AI Disruption Fears — Says Talks Of ‘SaaSpocalypse’ Overblown
key_facts: Chaudhry spoke to CNBC on Tuesday 6 Oct 2026, during Zscaler's Investor Day.
He called the 'SaaSpocalypse' talk overblown and said 'cyber is not keeping up'.
He said AI agents will be 'probably far more dangerous' weak links than users.
Zscaler reaffirmed fiscal 2027 revenue guidance of $3.908 billion to $3.938 billion, growth of 16.6% to 17.5% after 25% in fiscal 2026.
He said over half of Fortune 500 companies depend on Zscaler.
Zscaler shares are down over 8% this year while peers CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks have risen over 100%.
quote_evidence: Talking to CNBC on whether AI could replace companies such as Zscaler, Chaudhry said the talk of a "SaaSpocalypse" was overblown.
"Every CEO, every board is wanting to embrace AI, and what's holding back is lack of security."
why_it_matters_hint: A security chief argues AI raises demand for security rather than replacing software firms.
notes: Yahoo Finance carries a Stocktwits article ('originally published on StockTwits'); credited to Stocktwits, with CNBC as the interview source. Stocktwits URL not known; Yahoo link used.
